statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The post-close Broadcom sequence resolved with a completed retracement and near-flat index futures, so tail risk stays in the low band while stress remains elevated on the oil and yield regime.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window at 12:30Z-15:00Z on 3 September covering jobless claims, the trade balance, the U.S. cash open and ISM Services. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Broadcom reaction retraces and NQ futures hold flat; tail stays low with Thursday's ISM window flagged
body: As of the assessment, the Nasdaq-100 has closed at 29,143.33, up 0.23% inside a 28,972-29,166 session band, snapping a three-session losing streak. Broadcom reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year over year, with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion and Q4 guidance of about $34.8 billion; the shares initially dropped in the post-close reaction and had retraced to roughly -0.2% from the 367.24 close by 18:07 ET, while NQ futures held near flat around 29,141 inside a 28,927-29,213 range. That is a completed retracement rather than persistent directional efficiency, which is the observation that keeps tail risk in the low band even though the event was a high-impact single-name catalyst. VIX closed at 15.23, down 6.8%, near its session low. The latest H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.39%, the 10-year at 4.79% and the 30-year at 5.27%, with the 10-year having touched its highest level since 2023 during the week, and New York Fed President Williams described the yield move as reflecting strong economic prospects with no clear case yet for a September hike. Brent near $95 and WTI near $90 kept the energy premium in place after the recent escalation. Stress remains elevated because the oil shock, the yield level and the September FOMC debate are unresolved and the August payrolls report lands Friday. The next flagged window is Thursday 12:30Z-15:00Z, spanning jobless claims and the trade balance, the 13:30Z cash open and ISM Services at 14:00Z, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the pattern that changes the assessment.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment moved from a WATCH stretch in the event/whipsaw regime late on 1 September, through a trend-down phase during the European morning of 2 September as oil and yields drove the drawdown, into a steady green EA_ON de-escalation from about 12:00Z as the rebound produced two-way retracements, decaying volatility and a mixed dominant mode. Four clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued two-way price discovery with tail risk inside the low band overnight, followed by one narrow flagged window on Thursday at 12:30Z-15:00Z. That window stacks jobless claims and the July trade balance at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and ISM Services at 14:00Z, and it is the hour where an opening auction can convert an event impulse into continuation with shallow pullbacks. Conditional tail peaks in the watch band across 14:00Z-15:00Z and eases afterwards if retracements complete. Stress stays elevated to high throughout because the oil shock, the 10-year yield near its highest since 2023 and the September FOMC debate are unresolved, and it firms again late Thursday as Friday's payrolls approach. Confidence starts high on verified close, futures, volatility, rate, oil and earnings evidence and decays gradually with forecast distance.

forecast.analysis: Current hour. NDX closed at 29,143.33 (+0.23%) inside a 28,972-29,166 band, snapping a three-session skid. The Broadcom post-close drop had retraced to roughly -0.2% by 18:07 ET while NQ futures held near flat, so the results produced two-way discovery rather than one-way extension. Tail stays in the low band.

Contained overnight range is the working assumption for this hour

Two-way discovery assumed to persist into the European handoff

Watched pattern: directional extension without meaningful pullbacks

Conditional allowance for auction-window volatility rather than observed trend

Unresolved oil shock and 2023-high yields keep stress elevated

Persistent directional efficiency is the trigger, not a single large move
